title: GPU driver rollout Terraform module: health probes, graceful drain and upgrade hooks
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem statement: Upgrading GPU drivers and CUDA stacks in Private (VPC) clusters is high-risk for customer workloads. We currently lack a Terraform-first module that codifies safe rollout controls for both ASG-backed and Karpenter-managed GPU node groups. This ticket proposes a reusable terraform module that wires lifecycle hooks, health probes, and graceful-drain automation to reduce blast radius during driver and kernel-level upgrades.

Goals:
- Provide a module API that supports both AWS ASG+LaunchTemplate workflows and Karpenter Provisioners.
- Implement automatic canary nodes + controlled batch scale-down with graceful kube drain hooks before termination.
- Expose health-check endpoints and probe configuration so the console + alerting can detect regressions quickly.
- Integrate preflight checks (node readiness, driver version verification) and a post-upgrade validation job for inference runtimes (e.g., Triton/gRPC smoke tests).
- Ensure module is usable in Private VPC deployments with customer-managed networking and RBAC.

Constraints and non-goals:
- This module should not attempt to replace existing driver-install DaemonSets; it should coordinate with the on-cluster DaemonSet responsible for installing NVIDIA drivers.
- We will not implement a custom node image builder here; assume images are built by infra pipeline and versioned via launch template or provisioner constraints.

High-level design summary:
- ASG path: Terraform will create aws_autoscaling_group + aws_launch_template with lifecycle hooks. Lifecycle hook triggers an SNS -> SQS -> Lambda chain to run an SSM RunCommand on the instance to call a node-drain/health-check script. After successful drain and validation, lifecycle action completes.
- Karpenter path: Module will render a Karpenter Provisioner with a pod-eviction annotation and a weighted canary spec; we will use a ControllerJob (K8s Job) to mark provisioner weight and monitor node readiness and driver annotation before allowing scale down.
- Health probes: Module will provision an optional ServiceMonitor (Prometheus) yaml and configure an Inference runtime /health check route (configurable path and port) and create CloudWatch metrics or Prometheus metrics to power Console dashboards.
- Canary strategy: Default to 5% of target capacity (min 1 GPU node) as canary, then batch drain/upgrades in sizes configurable by percentage or absolute count.

Deliverables:
- Terraform module in modules/terraform/gpu-rollout with documented inputs/outputs.
- Example env overlay for Private deployment showing ASG and Karpenter usage.
- Automated test harness (GH action) that simulates node termination and asserts lifecycle hook completion.
- PRD and runbook linked in attachments.
acceptance_criteria: Module provides single API covering ASG and Karpenter modes (input: mode = "asg" | "karpenter")
On ASG mode, lifecycle hooks are created which delay instance termination until node-drain script completes and returns exit 0
On Karpenter mode, provisioner annotations and a controller Job ensure nodes are cordoned and drained before termination is allowed
Health probe configuration (path, port) is exposed and an example ServiceMonitor manifest is included
Module exposes canary_size and batch_size inputs; default canary_size=1 and batch_size=20%
CI tests simulate node termination and assert node drains and post-upgrade smoke tests succeed
Documentation includes rollout runbook and rollback steps; runbook reviewed by SRE and PM

2026-02-17 — Diego Marquez: Architecture sync notes: prefer SNS->SQS->Lambda to avoid tight coupling to ASG lifecycle hooks. Lambda will invoke SSM RunCommand to run the drain script. We should add a TTL for lifecycle hooks to avoid stuck terminations.
2026-02-24 — Sofia Chen: For Karpenter, we'll annotate nodes with "karpenter.sh/drain-initiator" and rely on eviction API; added a controller job to verify driver version post-provisioning.

2026-03-02 — Morgan Li: Security review requested. IAM roles for Lambda/SSM need scoping: ssm:SendCommand limited to instances with specific tags and lambda assume role restricted to module-managed resources.
2026-03-08 — Aisha Patel: Added acceptance criteria for CI simulation. QA will run in staging-east-2 Private cluster next week.

2026-03-12 — Diego Marquez: Pushed initial Terraform skeleton in branch feat/gpu-rollout. Created prototype lambda handler and basic lifecycle hook. Unit tests passing locally; integration tests failing on edge case where SSM agent is outdated on AMI. Investigating fallback strategy.
